sections.label: GDP growth and productivity
sections.summary: Developed economies' GDP growth has decelerated to 1% or lower, but Singapore can aim for 2% to 3% quality growth through productivity and labour force participation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Many developed economies going through the same experience have seen their annual gross domestic product (GDP) growth decelerate to 1% or lower.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We can aim for quality growth of 2% to 3%, if we press on in our drive for higher productivity and work hard to help everyone who wishes to work find a place in the labour force.

sections.label: GDP growth last year
sections.summary: Last year, GDP growth of 2.0% was achieved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last year, we achieved GDP growth of 2.0%1.

sections.label: Unemployment and redundancies
sections.summary: The unemployment rate remained low at 2.1% in 2016, but redundancies increased and more workers took longer to find jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Overall, unemployment rate remained low at 2.1%2 in 2016, but redundancies have been increasing and more workers are taking longer to find jobs.

sections.label: Levy deferral and infrastructure projects
sections.summary: Levy increases in two sectors will be deferred one more year, $700 million of public sector infrastructure projects brought forward, and construction foreign worker levy increases proceed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In view of the continued weaknesses, we will defer the earlier announced levy increases in these two sectors by one more year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support the construction sector, we will also bring forward $700 million worth of public sector infrastructure projects to start in financial year (FY) 2017 and FY2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To sustain the momentum for productivity improvement, we will proceed with the foreign worker levy increases for construction announced in 2015.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow worker support
sections.summary: MOM's "Adapt and Grow" initiative will get increased wage and training support, and an "Attach and Train" programme will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last year, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) launched the "Adapt and Grow" initiative to help workers looking to take on new jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will increase wage and training support provided under the Career Support Programme, the Professional Conversion Programme, and the Work Trial Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will introduce an "Attach and Train" programme for sectors that have good growth prospects, but where companies may not be ready to hire yet.

sections.label: Funding for worker initiatives
sections.summary: Up to $26 million a year will be committed from the Lifelong Learning Endowment Fund and the Skills Development Fund to support these initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: An additional sum of up to $26 million a year will be committed from the Lifelong Learning Endowment Fund and the Skills Development Fund to support these initiatives.

sections.label: Wage Credit Scheme payments
sections.summary: The Wage Credit Scheme will continue to help firms cope with rising wages, with over $600 million expected to be paid to businesses in March.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Wage Credit Scheme will continue to help firms cope with rising wages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We expect to pay over $600 million to businesses this March.

sections.label: Payouts benefiting 370,000 workers
sections.summary: Over $300 million will be paid out in FY2017, benefiting 370,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Over $300 million, which will benefit 370,000 workers, will be paid out in FY2017.

sections.label: Enhanced CIT rebate cap
sections.summary: The CIT rebate was enhanced from 30% to 50% of tax payable, capped at $20,000 for YA2016 and YA2017, and the cap will rise to $25,000 for YA2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last year, I enhanced the CIT rebate from 30% to 50% of tax payable, capped at $20,000 each year for Year of Assessment (YA) 2016 and YA2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, I will further enhance the CIT rebate by raising the cap from $20,000 to $25,000 for YA2017.

sections.label: SMEs Go Digital Programme
sections.summary: To strengthen enterprises, especially SMEs, the SMEs Go Digital Programme will be introduced to help SMEs build digital capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The first way to strengthen our enterprises, especially SMEs, is to help them adopt digital solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will introduce the SMEs Go Digital Programme to help SMEs build digital capabilities.

sections.label: Cybersecurity professional training funding
sections.summary: The Cyber Security Agency will work with professional bodies to train cybersecurity professionals, with more than $80 million made available for these programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Cyber Security Agency (CSA) of Singapore will work with professional bodies to train cybersecurity professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will make available more than $80 million for these programmes.

sections.label: A*STAR support for companies
sections.summary: A*STAR will expand its efforts to support 400 companies over the next four years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: A*STAR will expand its efforts to support 400 companies over the next four years.

sections.label: Extension to 36 months
sections.summary: In response to industry feedback, this will be extended to 36 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In response to industry feedback, this will be extended to 36 months.

sections.label: IE Singapore support and fund
sections.summary: IE Singapore supported companies in over 37,000 cases last year, and up to $600 million in Government capital will be committed for a new International Partnership Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last year, IE Singapore supported companies in over 37,000 cases, a 9% increase from 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To further support our firms to grow, we will continue to develop a smart financing ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will commit up to $600 million in Government capital for a new International Partnership Fund.

sections.label: Global Innovation Alliance setup
sections.summary: A Global Innovation Alliance will be set up for Singaporeans to gain overseas experience, build networks and collaborate with counterparts in other innovative cities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will now touch on two areas: new skills to operate overseas; and deepening skillsets to remain relevant on the job.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will set up a Global Innovation Alliance for Singaporeans to gain overseas experience, build networks and collaborate with their counterparts in other innovative cities.

sections.label: Innovators Academy student intake
sections.summary: The Innovators Academy will make opportunities available to students from other Singapore universities, growing annual intake from 300 to 500 over five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Innovators Academy will go further by making these opportunities available to students from other Singapore universities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We aim to grow the annual intake of students from 300 to 500 over the next five years.

sections.label: Alliance launch cities
sections.summary: In the initial phase, the Alliance will be launched in Beijing, San Francisco and various ASEAN cities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the initial phase, we will launch the Alliance in Beijing, San Francisco and various ASEAN cities.

sections.label: Leadership programme funding
sections.summary: The programme targets 800 potential leaders over three years, with $100 million set aside for the Global Innovation Alliance and Leadership Development Initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For a start, the programme will target to develop 800 potential leaders over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside $100 million to build capabilities under the Global Innovation Alliance and Leadership Development Initiative.

sections.label: Union course subsidies and fund
sections.summary: Union members can get subsidies for selected courses through the NTUC-Education and Training Fund, to which $150 million is set aside to match donations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In addition, union members can get subsidies for selected courses through the National Trades Union Congress-Education and Training Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have set aside $150 million to match donations to the Fund.

sections.label: Singtel cybersecurity training programme
sections.summary: Singtel trains its IT services employees for cybersecurity roles and works with CSA and IMDA on a programme for mid-career talent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Singtel not only trains its IT services employees to transition into cybersecurity roles, it also works with CSA and IMDA on the Cyber Security Associates and Technologists programme to develop mid-career talent for the broader cybersecurity industry.

sections.label: MAS venture capital framework
sections.summary: MAS has announced a simplified regulatory framework tailored to the needs of venture capital firms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For example, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has just announced a simplified regulatory framework tailored to the needs of venture capital firms.

sections.label: LTA self-driving vehicle zones
sections.summary: LTA has set out specific zones where self-driving vehicles can be tested on roads.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has done this with self-driving vehicles, setting out specific zones where they can be tested on roads.

sections.label: Public Sector Construction Productivity Fund
sections.summary: In the construction sector, a Public Sector Construction Productivity Fund with about $150 million will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For example, in the construction sector, we will introduce the Public Sector Construction Productivity Fund, with about $150 million.

sections.label: Top-ups and CFE funding
sections.summary: The National Research Fund is topped up by $500 million and the National Productivity Fund by $1 billion, with $2.4 billion set aside over four years for CFE strategies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In addition to the funding for the measures mentioned earlier, I will top up the National Research Fund by $500 million to support innovation efforts, and the National Productivity Fund by another $1 billion to support industry transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: All in, we are putting aside $2.4 billion over the next four years to implement the CFE strategies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In this way, our people will be constantly in touch with and be energised by new ideas, concepts, people, services and products from all over the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will continue to make significant investments in critical economic infrastructure, such as the new Changi Airport Terminal 5, the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail and the Tuas Terminal to deepen Singapore's connectivity to global markets.

sections.label: Punggol cybersecurity digital growth cluster
sections.summary: The upcoming Punggol growth cluster will co-locate cybersecurity and digital industries, with industry collaborating with the nearby Singapore Institute of Technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The upcoming growth cluster in Punggol will co-locate cybersecurity and digital industries, with industry collaborating closely with the nearby Singapore Institute of Technology.

sections.label: Singapore ratifies Paris Agreement
sections.summary: Singapore has joined more than 130 countries, including China, Japan and South Korea, in ratifying the Paris Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Singapore has joined more than 130 countries, including China, Japan and South Korea, in having ratified the Paris Agreement, reaffirming our commitment to address climate change and reduce emissions.

sections.label: Carbon tax on greenhouse gases
sections.summary: Singapore intends to implement a carbon tax on greenhouse gas emissions from 2019, applied upstream at $10 to $20 per tonne.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Singapore has studied this option for several years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We intend to implement a carbon tax on the emission of greenhouse gases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will consult widely with stakeholders and aim to implement the carbon tax from 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The tax will generally be applied upstream, for example, on power stations and other large direct emitters, rather than electricity users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We are looking at a tax rate of between $10 and $20 per tonne of greenhouse gas emissions.

sections.label: Road tax rebates diesel vehicles
sections.summary: Commercial diesel vehicles will receive a 100% road tax rebate for one year and partial rebate for two more years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To help businesses adjust, I will provide 100% road tax rebate for one year, and partial road tax rebate for another two years, for commercial diesel vehicles.

sections.label: New Vehicular Emissions Scheme
sections.summary: The Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme will be replaced by a Vehicular Emissions Scheme considering four other pollutants, running two years from 1 January 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The current Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme, or CEVS, was implemented in 2013 to encourage the take-up of cars and taxis with low carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will replace this with a new Vehicular Emissions Scheme, which will consider four other pollutants on top of carbon dioxide, so as to account more holistically for the health and environmental impact of vehicular emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The new Vehicular Emissions Scheme will run for two years, starting from 1 January 2018.

sections.label: Extension for commercial diesel vehicles
sections.summary: The scheme will be extended until 31 July 2019 for owners turning over Euro II and III commercial diesel vehicles for Euro VI vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As the scheme is due to expire on 31 July 2017, we will extend the scheme for vehicle owners who turn over their existing Euro II and III commercial diesel vehicles for Euro VI vehicles until 31 July 2019, and further enhance the COE bonus period for Light Goods Vehicles.

sections.label: Water price increase
sections.summary: Water prices will increase by 30% in two phases starting 1 July 2017 to reflect latest water supply costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We need to update our water prices to reflect the latest costs of water supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will increase water prices by 30% in two phases, starting from 1 July 2017.

sections.label: Business increase impact
sections.summary: For three-quarters of businesses, the increase will be less than $25 per month once fully phased in on 1 July 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For three-quarters of our businesses, the increase will be less than $25 per month, once the increase is fully phased in on 1 July 2018.

sections.label: CPF Housing Grant increase
sections.summary: CPF Housing Grant rises to $50,000 for 4-room or smaller resale flats and $40,000 for 5-room or bigger, costing $110 million yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: With immediate effect, we will increase the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Housing Grant from $30,000 to $50,000 for couples who purchase 4-room or smaller resale flats, and from $30,000 to $40,000 for couples who purchase 5-room or bigger resale flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Together with the Additional CPF Housing Grant and Proximity Housing Grant13, a couple can now receive a total of up to $110,000 in housing grants when buying a resale flat, depending on the flat location, flat type and their income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Other eligible first-timers will also benefit from some grant enhancement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This measure will cost an additional $110 million per year.

sections.label: Infant care capacity increase
sections.summary: Centre-based infant care capacity will increase to over 8,000 places by 2020 to meet growing demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To meet growing demand, we will increase the capacity of centre-based infant care to over 8,000 places by 2020.

sections.label: Student fee increase amounts
sections.summary: Increases are up to $400 for undergraduates, $350 for diploma students and $200 for ITE students, benefiting about 12,000 more Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The amount of increase will be up to $400 for undergraduate students, up to $350 for diploma students, and up to $200 for ITE students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: About 12,000 more Singaporean students are expected to benefit, bringing the total number of beneficiaries to 71,000.

sections.label: Third Enabling Masterplan launch
sections.summary: The Third Enabling Masterplan, put together by a committee of private and public sector representatives, will be launched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Under the two previous Masterplans, we increased support in areas, such as early intervention and education, employment, care services, assistive technologies and accessibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will launch the Third Enabling Masterplan, which was put together by a committee of private and public sector representatives.

sections.label: Disability caregiver support spending
sections.summary: A Disability Caregiver Support Centre will be set up, with around $400 million yearly spent on initiatives for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To support caregivers, we will set up a Disability Caregiver Support Centre to provide information, planned respite, training and peer support groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Including existing initiatives, we expect to spend around $400 million per year on initiatives supporting persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Community mental health funding
sections.summary: An additional $160 million will be spent on Community Mental Health efforts over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As part of our Community Mental Health efforts, we will spend an additional $160 million in the next five years.

sections.label: Funding for VWOs and charities
sections.summary: Up to $100 million in additional funding over five years will develop the capabilities of VWOs and charities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Over the next five years, we will provide additional funding, up to $100 million in total, to further develop the capabilities of our VWOs and charities.

sections.label: Cultural Matching Fund top-up
sections.summary: The Cultural Matching Fund will be topped up by $150 million to sustain momentum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To sustain this momentum, I will top up the Cultural Matching Fund by $150 million.

sections.label: Healthcare, transport and MRT spending
sections.summary: Healthcare spending more than doubled to around $10 billion in FY2016, and almost doubling the MRT network by 2030 will cost over $20 billion in five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Over the last five years, our annual healthcare spending has more than doubled to around $10 billion in FY2016 as we enhanced subsidies and expanded healthcare services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Healthcare spending will continue to rise as our population ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will also continue to enhance our public transport infrastructure, almost doubling the MRT network by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This will put eight in 10 households within a 10-minute walk of a rail station.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This alone is expected to cost the Government more than $20 billion over the next five years.

sections.label: Permanent budget cap adjustment
sections.summary: A permanent 2% downward adjustment to budget caps of all Ministries and Organs of State applies from FY2017 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We can do better, and more, with less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will apply a permanent 2% downward adjustment to the budget caps of all Ministries and Organs of State from FY2017 onwards, to emphasise the need to stay prudent and effective.

sections.label: Rising expenditures and taxes
sections.summary: Longer-term expenditures will rise with healthcare and infrastructure investment, requiring new taxes or higher tax rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Domestically, we will also face rising expenditures over the longer term as we invest more in healthcare and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will have to raise revenues through new taxes or raise tax rates.

sections.label: FY2016 budget surplus
sections.summary: For FY2016, a budget surplus of $5.2 billion, or 1.3% of GDP, is expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For FY2016, we expect a budget surplus of $5.2 billion, or 1.3% of GDP.

sections.label: FY2017 budget position
sections.summary: Ministries' expenditures are expected to be $3.7 billion, or 5.2%, higher than FY2016, with a smaller FY2017 surplus of $1.9 billion, or 0.4% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Ministries' expenditures are expected to be $3.7 billion, or 5.2%, higher than in FY2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Overall, a smaller budget surplus of $1.9 billion, or 0.4% of GDP, is expected in FY2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As we expect expenditures to continue rising in the long term, this budget position is prudent, while supporting firms and households in the midst of continued economic restructuring.

sections.label: Budget 2017 environmental measures
sections.summary: Budget 2017 reaffirms keeping Singapore vibrant, studying a carbon tax, changing diesel tax structure, adjusting vehicle schemes, raising water price, and supporting lower-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Budget 2017 also reaffirms our commitment to keep Singapore a vibrant city with a quality living environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will study a carbon tax, change the tax structure for diesel and adjust vehicle incentive schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will also increase the price of water to reflect the latest costs of water supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: At the same time, we will provide support to lower-income households.

sections.label: Parliament debate adjournment
sections.summary: The Question seeks Parliament's approval of the Government's financial policy for 1 April 2017 to 31 March 2018, and the debate stands adjourned.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the financial year 1 April 2017 to 31 March 2018." In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.
